claude.performance_metric: $3.2bn goodwill impairment (Q2 2020); segment FY2020 net sales -26%, operating profit -67% vs FY2019, then recovery to $20,597m sales / 11.4% margin by FY2022
claude.rationale: The slice attributes the FY2020 sales/profit decline and $3.2bn goodwill impairment principally to the COVID-19 pandemic's effect on commercial-aerospace flight hours, OEM deliveries, and aftermarket demand, plus restructuring tied to the separate Raytheon Merger — not to any misalignment of the acquired product line with operating processes, so no product/process disruption is documented (p4=0). No integration fracture between operations and the acquired organization's people/management/culture is documented; the disruptions cited are exogenous demand shocks and merger-related restructuring, so p5=0. The segment recovered through FY2022 (net sales $20,597m, operating margin 11.4%), and no evidence of business-model incompatibility (t2=0); the slice discloses nothing about the controlling-intent archetype's realized coherence (t1=uncertain).

grok.rationale: The slice attributes the Collins Aerospace segment's FY2020 net-sales (−26%) and operating-profit (−67%) collapse, plus the $3.2bn goodwill impairment, to COVID-19 commercial-aerospace demand shocks and to restructuring tied to the concurrent Raytheon Merger, not to any realized inability to align acquired products with operating processes. No evidence is given of operations-versus-organization/culture fracture over the 3–5-year horizon; the segment is described as continuing and recovering through FY2022 on air-traffic rebound. Absence of documented product/process or process/organization disruption therefore codes both pathways 0.

openai.rationale: No realized product/process-interface disruption is documented; the FY2020 sales and profit declines were attributed principally to pandemic-driven reductions in commercial aerospace demand, followed by recovery through FY2022. No process/organization fracture is documented; although restructuring at Collins Aerospace contributed to 2020 results, the filing ties those actions to the subsequent Raytheon Merger and does not describe operations breaking against people, management, or culture.
